title: How To Get Into Detox for Drugs and Alcohol
h1: How To Get Into Detox for Drugs and Alcohol
metaDescription: By figuring out how to get into detox for drugs and alcohol, you’re increasing your chances of being able to successfully create a life in long-term recovery. Learn how we can help you overcome your addiction.

blocks.text: You’ve decided to get sober. Now, what do you do? While choosing to get sober is the best decision you can make for your future self, it results in a list of other choices. The good news is that you do not have to make them all at once. Make one decision at a time, and also know that you can adjust as you move forward. The first decision to make is whether or not you need to go to detox. You’ll have to take an honest look at how much alcohol and drugs you have been using and how often. Suppose you are a daily user or daily drinker. In that case, you will want to go to detox for your safety. Detoxing from drugs and alcohol without medical supervision is dangerous and can be fatal. Once you’ve decided to go to detox, you’ll need to find out how to get into detox. At Marina Harbor Detox, we know the strength required to choose to get sober and then do the work. We have the tools to best support you through detox safely and then help you set up a plan to build a life in recovery.
What Is Detox for Drugs and Alcohol?

When you use drugs and alcohol regularly, your body adjusts to this and changes how it functions. When you stop, your body begins to go through acute withdrawal. Depending on how much and how often you have been using, withdrawal symptoms can start as soon as four hours after your last drug or drink. Withdrawal symptoms will vary according to your drug or drugs of choice, but you can expect to feel anxious, agitated, and tired. Detox is the bridge between actively using and beginning your sobriety journey.

First, you have to rid your body of drugs and alcohol so that you can start the work of long-term recovery. Your job is to figure out how to get into detox and then get yourself there. The rest of the decisions can be made when the toxins have been flushed out of your system. During detox, medical professionals will monitor your overall health, including your blood pressure, heart rate, and other indicators, to assess the severity of your withdrawal symptoms. Using this assessment, detox professionals can administer supportive medications to manage your symptoms and prevent you from experiencing the more severe symptoms.
How Do I Know if I Need Detox?

Whether or not you need detox is almost entirely dependent on what drugs you have been using and how often you have been using. You are going to need to be honest with yourself about your drug and alcohol use. While alcohol is socially accepted, it is one of the most dangerous substances from which to withdraw. Likewise, benzodiazepines like Xanax and Valium are also hazardous during withdrawal without medical supervision. Going to detox also allows you to have your symptoms managed by medical professionals in a supportive environment without the ability to go use.

Withdrawal can be very stressful for our bodies. You may experience headaches, sweating, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and muscle cramps. If you drink alcohol or use drugs like Xanax regularly, you also are at risk for severe withdrawal symptoms such as delirium tremens or seizures, which can be fatal. Many who have tried to quit using drugs and alcohol have great difficulty overcoming the physical aspects of the withdrawal process without returning to drugs and alcohol. Sadly, each time we put our bodies through withdrawal, we increase the stress we’re putting on our bodies. By figuring out how to get into detox and going there, you can protect your health and increase your chances of successfully moving onto sobriety. The goal of medical detox is to get you through withdrawal as safely as possible to begin your recovery journey.

Withdrawal isn’t fun, but it is necessary. At Marina Harbor Detox, we know just how dangerous and challenging withdrawal can be. Our team of medical professionals understands what it takes to detox safely and recover from addiction. We provide a luxurious, intimate setting that relies on individualized care and a low patient-to-staff ratio. In addition, we will provide you with a structured, supportive environment to enable you to create life in long-term recovery. So contact us today and let us keep you safe while you detox from drugs and alcohol.
